ledger.note: 605: Rajyavardhana defeats Devagupta and Malwa is lost. "He defeated Devagupta, Mahasenagupta's son and successor in Malwa, 'in 605'"; the page calls Rajyavardhana "of Kannauj" (he was of Thanesar, the Pushyabhuti dynasty, whose brother Harsha is mentioned only as a companion of Mahasenagupta's sons). Rajyavardhana was Harsha's elder brother (Harsha page: Prabhakaravardhana died in 605 and Rajyavardhana succeeded), so pushyabhuti-dynasty may be the early years of harsha-s-empire (Cliopatria 612-655); sa-03 should decide before a dossier is made.

ledger.note: c. 606: Magadha returns to the Later Guptas. "Harsha (c. 606-647 CE) restored Later Gupta rule in Magadha" (Later Gupta page, no year; Harsha's coronation April 606 on the Harsha page, which does not name the Later Guptas). Counterpart changed from nobody to the Maukharis, who took Magadha in 575 (/ledger above): the Mahasenagupta page has Sharvavarman of Kannauj "conquering a part of the already crumbling empire of Magadha" and Kirttivarman I of the Chalukya family subduing Magadha (neither dated) and names no ruler of Magadha after 575, so the holder at 606 is the researcher's reading; if sa-03 finds that Harsha held it, the counterpart is harsha-s-empire. The year is Harsha's accession year: a bridge.

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks (sa-02-d suggested it for sa-02-x or sa-03; Cliopatria draws the Gupta Empire in Magadha to 554 and nothing after). Three pages opened (budget 2-5). The life 490-750 runs mostly in the sa-03 period: sa-03 batches should check this dossier against maukhari-dynasty, harsha-s-empire, gauda-kingdom and kannauj-varman-dynasty. Dates: the two pages disagree on the Mahasenagupta reign (list c. 562-601, which includes Malwa; Magadha 562-575 on his own page); the Kalachuri page puts the Maitraka loss of Ujjain at 616-617 in a footnote, against 597 here. 606 and 655 are confidence-1 bridges. The ruler list is the page's; Kumaragupta II (601), Devagupta (601-605) and Madhavagupta (601-655) overlap on it, and the strip is given as Magadha line from 606. Not drawn: Shashanka (vassal who left Mahasenagupta, undated), Kirttivarman I's subjugation of Magadha (undated, Mahasenagupta page). Gazetteer names needed: Pataliputra (alias of Patna), Gomati (river). REPAIR (2026-10-19, after review): (1) the 606-749 keyframe is split: Magadha 606-654, the Bihar-Jharkhand-West Bengal union from 655 (the ledger gain of 655 is reduced to the land beyond Magadha); (2) the Mahishmati disc (75.6 E, 22.2 N, 100 km) that kalachuris-of-mahishmati holds from 550 is subtracted from the Malwa keyframes, the 575 gain, the 597 loss, the 605 loss and the 605 war zone (84 and 41 cells; Ujjain's own disc loses 43); (3) vassal events added in the vassal's-own-ledger direction (counterpart = suzerain, the mirror the reviewer asked for): gupta-empire 490-525 (confidence 2/1; 525 is Jivitagupta I's accession, the first claim of independence on the page, not the reviewer's c. 550) and harsha-s-empire 606-647 (confidence 2/1); the 606 gain now names maukhari-dynasty (confidence 1) as the 575 loss did; (4) capital Ujjain ends 596 and Vidisha is a flagged stand-in for 597-605. Not changed: /ledger counterpart pushyabhuti-dynasty (note added: it may be harsha-s-empire's early years; sa-03 to decide). Thin gaps: the Adityasena page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adityasena and /Adityasena_Gupta) could not be read, so the 655 widening stays at confidence 1; the Harsha page does not name the Later Guptas and dates only his coronation (April 606). Routing for other owners: gupta-empire (vassal events 490-525 with counterpart later-gupta-dynasty), harsha-s-empire (vassal events 606-647), maukhari-dynasty (loss of Magadha in 606 if it held it), kalachuris-of-mahishmati (its 597 gain of Ujjain overlaps its own Mahishmati disc by 43 cells).
